newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: GM says still interested in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: GM says still interested in Philippines.

text.p: General Motors Corp (GM) said on Monday it was still interested in pursuing talks with the Philippines even as local officials said they were not keen on relaxing investment rules to accommodate the U.S. car giant.

"Our discussions with both the BOI (Board of Investments) and DTI (Department of Trade and Industry) will continue as we try to determine what level of investment and activity in the Philippines would be appropriate," Erhard Spranger, executive director of General Motors Asian & Pacific operations, said in a conference.

Earlier, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said GM had wanted to set up a car components facility under the Motor Vehicle Development Programme. The programme accords cheaper tariff rates for stripped car parts.
One of the requirements of the programme, however, was that the company should set up an assembly plant in the country.
Bautista said GM wanted a car components facility in the Philippines prior to setting up an assembly plant.
The Philippines lost last year to Thailand as the site of a major GM manufacturing plant for the Asia Pacific region.
GM officials declined to give specifics regarding its talks with local investment officials.
